posts.author: atolmasoff
posts.body:
Hi all! Been working on a game, so far so good. Recently I'm getting to a point where I'd like to focus on animations. In the process of seeing how to get in custom ones, I've found an issue:
Whenever I go into animations tab, maybe 30% of the time it'll lock up and crash. Other times it loads, but if I click on other animations to quickly, or scroll around too fast, it freezes and crashes.  Happens with this project, or brand new one. Re-installed GFX drivers, re-installed MZ, but still crashing.
The goal is to replace RTP animations with ones for my game, so they've not been touched. Using Visuastella_base and _combat, but happens with or without the plugins.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
what is your editor version, and what is your project core version?
it might be that your project core is an older version than the editor, and there was an update to include MV-style animations that will cause problems if it is not present in both editor and core.
where did you store the project?
that behaviour can also be caused if the editor has problems accessing and loading the animation file, for example if it was stored in a cloud folder and you currently have a slow internet.
or a few other causes that can usually be seen in the full folderpath to the project (the one beginning with the drive letter, usually "c:\users\user\...."

that does not check for files added to a folder, and with your previous answers that is most likely that cause:
at one time in the past you added a damaged or otherwise wrong file to that folder, and now the editor crashes as soon as it tries to read that file.
if you make a new project, does the animation tab work in that project? do not add anything custom to it.
if yes, close the editor and compare the two animation folders of both projects. Move all files that are in the damaged project folder but not in the new project folder to a backup folder anywhere else.
then test. if it works, move the files from the backup folder back one after another, testing after each file if that is the damaged one.
if it does not work, one of the base files must have become damaged, simply copy everything from the working project folder into the damaged project folder and test again.

posts.author: Erif
posts.body:
MV had a weird issue with memory that caused a similar crash. It also ocurred with the animations tab. So, Investigating, there's a fix that expands MV's virtual memory limit from 2GB to 4GB (It's the easiest I can explain without going into more technical aspects). I don't know if this is fixed with MZ, so you can try it anyways.
4GB Patch – NTCore
ntcore.com
The instructions are included in the post of the tool, I have used it myself and a few close friends with MV. Perhaps it may be useful?
PD: If you have MZ in Steam you have to patch the executable in the steamapps/common/RPG Maker MZ folder, not the direct access.

posts.author: DismasRichter
posts.body:
I was having this issue some time ago, and after doing some research, in my case I found out it was caused by a faulty DLL:
"C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\uXXXXXXX.inf_amd64_XXXXXXXXXXXX\BXXXXXX\atio6axx.dll"
This DLL is related to OpenGL, and the only way I found to fix the problem was by reverting to an older driver version. In my case, I rolled back to WHQL version 24.7.1.
My recommendation, (especially if your GPU is from AMD) is doing the same. Since then, I haven't had any crashes at all. Comparing it to the video you posted, the issue on my end happened in exactly the same way.
